source.title: Large Scale Structure of Neural Network Loss Landscapes

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures loss-landscape geometry and discusses its possible relation to generalization, but reports no training-versus-test error gaps or results on the claim versions. Its cited generalization findings are prior work.
record.gate_note: The paper reports how learning rate, batch size, L2 regularization, and dropout rate change radial low-loss tunnel width. These are geometric measurements, not results on the training/test generalization gap. Its SWA comparison concerns ensembling performance, not the claim's generalization versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures loss-landscape geometry and ensembling behavior. It does not compare held-out performance for the interventions in V1–V6 or V8, or relate magnitude-aware sharpness to generalization gaps as required by V7. Its discussion of curvature and generalization relies on prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors propose and experimentally investigate a high-dimensional wedge model of loss landscapes, demonstrate connectors among multiple optima, relate landscape dimensionality to intrinsic optimization dimension, and show hyperparameter effects on radial tunnel width. They also demonstrate learning-rate-dependent failures of stochastic weight averaging. They do not directly test the listed generalization versions.
record.recipe_differences: Measures loss-landscape geometry and connectivity rather than testing the listed generalization interventions or outcomes.
record.method_sensitivity: Tunnel width changes with learning rate, batch size, L2 regularization strength, and dropout rate; L2 and dropout effects disappear at sufficiently strong settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Higher learning rate, L2 regularization and dropout widen radial low-loss tunnels; larger batches narrow them. The widening effects disappear at excessive L2 or dropout strengths.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training hyperparameters influence the geometry of the low-loss regions reached by a CNN on CIFAR-10.

fits_no_version.finding: With sufficiently high cyclical learning rates, snapshots occupy different wedges and their averaged weights perform worse than individual snapshots; lower learning rates permit effective weight averaging.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The effectiveness of stochastic weight averaging depends on whether snapshots remain within a shared low-loss region.

record.problems: The reported hyperparameter results are described qualitatively with values shown only in Figure 5; no uncertainty estimates are stated. The paper says it explored other architectures and datasets but does not present those results in plots.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant results were reported. The SWA ensemble comparison in Figure 6 concerns weight averaging and ensemble predictions, not the generalization-gap outcomes in the versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy under matched recipes.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under specified tuning, decay, or switching conditions.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error, including small datasets, excessive dropout, and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps, including comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Held-out accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The row states describe interpretability against the claim versions, not whether the geometric findings occurred. The supplied text includes test-loss visualizations and ensembling performance, so lack of relevance should not be described as a complete absence of held-out measurements.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test performance.
Test error as network width grows beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected test error and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer held-out performance under different tuning and decay choices.
Large-batch versus small-batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across training-set sizes and augmentation settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of training/test gaps against other measures.
Effect on test accuracy of removing memorized examples and retraining.

rows.subject: SimpleCNN
rows.operation_detail: Measured radial low-loss tunnel angular width across learning rates.
rows.measure: Angular width of radial low-loss tunnels.
rows.note: The text states that higher learning rate yields wider tunnels; numerical values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: Higher learning rates widen radial tunnels, but tunnel width alone cannot establish any listed version.

rows.subject: SimpleCNN
rows.operation_detail: Measured radial low-loss tunnel angular width across batch sizes.
rows.measure: Angular width of radial low-loss tunnels.
rows.note: Larger batch size leads to narrower tunnels, according to the text; numerical values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: Narrower tunnels with larger batches do not establish worse held-out performance under V5. Section 4.4 states this result, but Figure 5's caption identifies learning rate, L2 regularization and dropout, not batch size; the figure-only attribution is unsupported by the supplied text.

rows.subject: SimpleCNN
rows.operation_detail: Measured radial low-loss tunnel angular width across L2 regularization strengths.

conditions.value: higher; effect disappears when too strong

rows.measure: Angular width of radial low-loss tunnels.
rows.note: Higher L2 regularization widens tunnels up to a point; the effect disappears when regularization is too strong.
rows.check: L2 regularization widens tunnels until its strength becomes excessive. This geometric result does not measure any listed version's effect.

rows.subject: SimpleCNN
rows.operation_detail: Measured radial low-loss tunnel angular width across dropout rates.

conditions.value: higher; effect disappears when too high

rows.measure: Angular width of radial low-loss tunnels.
rows.note: Higher dropout rate widens tunnels up to a point; the effect disappears when the rate is too high.
rows.check: Dropout widens tunnels until its rate becomes excessive. This does not establish lower held-out error or underfitting under V6.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
